episodes.210633: A shower produced localized gale-force winds over the tidal Patuxent River.
episodes.211001: Both on the evening of the 30th and late afternoon of the 31st, the southeast TX Panhandle was impacted by severe storms that formed as a small complex. Each day looked very similar on radar. These storms produced wind gusts up to 64 mph and hail up to the size of quarters on the 30th. On the 31st the storms did produce hail up to quarters but no wind gusts were recorded.
episodes.211055: On the afternoon of the 30th, a dryline moved back into the Rolling Plains of West Texas allowing for low level moisture to surge into the region. Areas on the caprock saw scattered high based showers and thunderstorms generating severe wind gusts over Lubbock and Floyd Counties. Stronger moisture in the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle allowed for more robust thunderstorms. These storms produced severe wind gusts as well as hail as large as golf ball size in the city of Memphis (Hall County).
episodes.211226: A persistent, slow-moving trough remained over the American Samoa islands between March 26 and March 30. WFO American Samoa recorded a total of 5.45 inches of rainfall during this time. This led to saturated soils that triggered multiple landslides across the territory.

events.county: Patuxent River To Broomes Island Md
events.narrative: Wind gusts of up to 36 knots (42 MPH) were measured by the Solomons Island NOS sensor (SLIM2).
A landslide was reported at Poloa Village on the morning of March 30, scattering debris and rocks across the main road. No injuries were reported.
A 58mph wind gust was measured from a shower near the Goodnight mesonet site.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Shallowater measured severe wind gusts from 1623 CST through 1638 CST. A peak wind gust of 72 mph was measured at 1638 CST.
The Automated Surface Observing System at Lubbock International Airport measured severe wind gusts from 1700 CST through 1708 CST.
Significant flooding occurred on Indian Creek, which was over 100 yards wide and likely 12 feet deep during the peak of the flooding. The flooding washed out ranch fencing in the area.
Hail fell southwest of Hedley for about an hour and a half. Hail ranged from dime to quarter size, although damage occurred to skylights which would suggest that some larger hailstones also fell.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell and accumulated. Hail fell for at least 15 minutes.
A tree broke on Blair Street and the roof was partially blown off a trailer house on Adamson Street.
Pea to quarter size hail fell in Samnorwood.
